paragraphs.zh: 虚构读者准备一次小型拼图聚会，先列两种日期，等参与者确认后才预约房间；另一次他先读完场地规则再发邀请。两种速度都可能服务准备，不能由出生落点判定哪一种更勇敢。
paragraphs.en: A fictional reader offers two dates for a puzzle gathering and waits for replies before booking a room. On another occasion, reading the venue rules before inviting anyone is useful. Both paces can serve preparation; a birth position establishes neither as braver.

paragraphs.zh: 可以借开场主题问：“这一步只是在探询，还是会替别人承诺？谁还需要选择？”只谈虚构计划，不比较朋友谁更主动。
paragraphs.en: Use the beginning theme to ask whether a step explores an option or commits someone else, and who still needs a choice. Discuss the fictional plan without ranking friends by initiative.

paragraphs.en: A fictional reader checking a public garden’s opening hours becomes curious about its name. Confirming today’s entrance can come first while the history remains open. Pausing a branch proves no lack of curiosity; a missing answer establishes no lack of ability.

paragraphs.en: An optional card separates a fact needed today, an interesting branch and what remains unverified. Read without pursuing private details or competing over knowledge.

paragraphs.en: A fictional reader thinks a library entrance has moved; checking shows only the sign moved. On another occasion, the entrance really changed. A new angle can revise or support an initial account without producing a revelation every time.

paragraphs.en: An optional card asks what the invitation explains, which forms of participation are optional and how it ends. Liveliness, duration and photographs establish neither affection nor charm.

paragraphs.en: Fictional readers take turns returning a shared key each week and revise the handoff when schedules change. Revision does not automatically damage trust, and uninterrupted continuation does not prove both still have a free choice.

paragraphs.en: Ask when an agreement ends and when it can be discussed again. Compare concrete tasks without inferring marriage suitability, loyalty or a permanent duty to support someone.

paragraphs.en: A fictional reader folds a paper box and sees the creases more clearly after changing the light; another attempt benefits from a demonstration. Task, tools and support change an experience without establishing talent or bodily worth.

paragraphs.en: Ask which aim remains, which facts are provisional and what information would change the plan. Writing is enough; no winning, promised concession or demonstration of strength is required.

paragraphs.en: A fictional reader summarizes public venue instructions and discovers that one day in advance refers to cancellation rather than arrival. Accurate reception can require text, a pause or another question without establishing hearing, wisdom or obedience.

paragraphs.en: A fictional reader joins a weekly book swap where one regular collection notice suffices and extra reminders bury the location. Others can reply later or skip it. Synchrony does not measure commitment; fewer signals can be clearer.

paragraphs.en: An optional card asks about start, pause and finish signals, who may miss them and how to request a change. Drum imagery imposes no shared pace and grades neither musical nor social ability.

paragraphs.en: A fictional reader publishes an event checklist with location and supplies while keeping contact numbers restricted to their agreed purpose. Distribution follows use, not a verdict about mystery, isolation, trustworthiness or a need for healing.

paragraphs.en: Borrow the circle theme to ask who needs which information, why and when the need ends. Use harmless project details rather than health, another person’s secrets or private history.

paragraphs.en: A fictional reader borrows a room for one games session, names this entrance and the next update date, and promises no permanent venue. Temporary arrangements may suffice or need alternatives; uncertainty predicts neither crisis, loss nor spiritual transformation.

paragraphs.en: A fictional reader compares requests for larger exhibition text and fuller explanations, checks dimensions, content and use, then considers layered versions. Two viewpoints do not make factual claims equally supported or require compromise every time.

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“共同事实、不同需要、未核实假设各是什么？”只用实际表达，不代演他人内心，也不把双视角说成欺骗、分裂或隐藏真我。
paragraphs.en: Ask about common facts, different needs and unverified assumptions. Use expressed views without impersonating another mind or treating two perspectives as deception, division or a hidden true self.

paragraphs.en: These additional scenes and conversation cards are original FermatMind Editorial material for optional reading or fictional discussion, not traditional personality rules, a personality test or instructions to act. Resonance does not validate a birth star; mismatch establishes no personal fault. Read astronomical positions, cultural categories and real-life evidence separately. Adjacent readings remain separate near a boundary, without a hybrid personality or compatibility ranking. All 27 guides need no birth details. Copying includes only the public calculator and all guide URLs, without birth time, zone or coordinates.

paragraphs.zh: 虚构读者结束共享食谱草稿，标出已核实步骤、待补图片与下一位编辑可找的材料。留下问题仍可以完成一次交接，结束自己的任务不承诺永久待命，也不能保证未来结果。
paragraphs.en: A fictional reader hands over a shared recipe draft with checked steps, missing images and locations of materials for its next editor. Open questions can remain after a handoff. Ending one task promises neither permanent availability nor a guaranteed outcome.

paragraphs.zh: 可选卡：“已完成、仍开放、下一条有用信息、自己的责任终点。”只谈普通任务，不用鼓的比喻决定关系何时结束或预测旅途安全。
paragraphs.en: An optional card names done, still open, the next useful information and the end of one’s responsibility. Discuss ordinary tasks; drum imagery decides neither relationship endings nor travel safety.
